entries.snippet: The Council of Europe awarded human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh with the Vaclav Havel human rights prize. She is a prominent advocate for the rights of women, children and political prisoners.

entries.title: Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
entries.snippet: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

entries.title: Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
entries.snippet: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

entries.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?

entries.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
entries.snippet: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW has more.

entries.title: Hungary lifts PM Peter Magyar’s immunity, clears way for probes into 2 former Orban ministers
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has backed the move himself. Two former ministers who served under his rival Viktor Orban now face separate corruption probes.

entries.title: Pope decries 'scourge' of sexual abuse during France visit

entries.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe

entries.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?

entries.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
entries.snippet: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

entries.title: Sweden faces political deadlock after election-winning center-left bloc fails to form government
entries.snippet: Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson has abandoned efforts to form a four-party government. Deep divisions within the election-winning bloc have left Sweden in political deadlock.

entries.title: India: LPU suspends classes after violent protests over alleged campus rape
entries.snippet: A university in Punjab has suspended classes after protests over a rumored sexual assault took a violent turn. Separately, the Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognizance of recent rape cases in Delhi.

entries.title: Venezuelans demand opposition leader Machado's return
entries.snippet: Hundreds of people held rallies in Venezuela demanding the safe return of Maria Corina Machado, and fair elections.

entries.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
entries.snippet: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

entries.title: Ukraine, South Korea relations sour over North Korean POWs

entries.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats of status in West Bank
entries.snippet: The move by the Israeli Foreign Ministry is a response to Dutch sanctions targeting goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The Dutch Foreign Ministry is yet to comment.

entries.title: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic announces resignation
entries.snippet: Aleksandar Vucic will now be running to be prime minister in the upcoming snap parliamentary elections slated for next month.
